name: Rhythm & Sound
editorial_article:
Rhythm & Sound is an influential Berlin-based electronic music project comprised of Moritz von Oswald and Mark Ernestus. Emerging in the late 1990s as a departure from their legendary work under the Basic Channel moniker, Rhythm & Sound stripped back the icy, machine-driven textures of Detroit-influenced techno in favor of a profound, meditative exploration of traditional Jamaican dub. Operating their own eponymous label and the Burial Mix imprint—both distributed through the iconic Hardwax store—the duo crafted a sound defined by cavernous, enveloping basslines, sparse percussion, and a signature "crackle" that evokes the physical degradation of classic vinyl.

Their output, frequently featuring collaborations with vocalists like Paul St. Hilaire (often credited as Tikiman) and Shalom, bridged the gap between electronic dance music and roots reggae with uncanny precision. Unlike the more propulsive, rhythmic complexity of Basic Channel, Rhythm & Sound focused on hypnotic repetition, deep atmospheric space, and emotional resonance. Their albums and 10-inch singles remain essential blueprints for the dub-techno subgenre, influencing generations of producers who seek to marry the heavy-weight bass culture of Jamaica with the minimalist, post-industrial landscape of Berlin. Their legacy is characterized by an uncompromising commitment to sonic detail, anonymous presentation, and a timeless, subterranean gravity.
